newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: British Airways/Comair cut S.African fares.
newsitem.headline: British Airways/Comair cut S.African fares.

text.p: British Airways/Comair, the largest privately owned airline in South Africa, said on Monday it would slash fares on some of its routes with immediate and continuous effect.
Comair, as the airline used to be known, entered into a franchise agreement with British Airways that came into effect on Sunday.

It said in a statement the routes on which return fares would be slashed were Johannesburg to/from Cape Town, Port Elizabeth, Durban and Richards Bay; Cape Town/Port Elizabeth, Durban/Port Elizabeth and Durban/Cape Town.
"These prices are 15 percent lower than when we started the Johannesburg/Cape Town route in 1991," Comair commercial director Bert van der Linden said.
He said South African Airways and other government-owned airlines had 90 percent of the domestic airline market and by slashing fares, Comair would capture additional market share.
